description: An editorial magazine for architecture and real-estate enthusiasts that tracks notable properties through a kanban-style deal pipeline — from 'Just Listed' to 'Sold' — with long-form reporting on each one

pages.name: board
pages.description: Kanban-style watchlist that tracks notable listed properties across pipeline stages
components: Top masthead with the publication name on the left, a horizontal section nav (The Board, Dossiers, Neighborhoods, Archive, About), and a right cluster with a search input and a 'Sign in' link
Sub-header strip showing the current issue label, a market filter dropdown (city), a price-band chip row, a property-type chip row, and a 'Reset filters' text button

Five-column kanban board with columns Just Listed, Open House, Under Offer, In Escrow, Closed — each column has a title, a count badge, and a stack of property cards (thumbnail, address, price, bed/bath/sqft, days-on-market chip)
Right-rail panel titled 'This week on the board' listing five recently-moved properties with a tiny arrow indicating which column they moved from and to, plus a timestamp
Footer with a four-column site map (Sections, Markets, Newsletter, Masthead), a weekly-digest email sign-up form, and a copyright line

pages.name: dossier
pages.description: Long-form editorial dossier on a single property pulled from the board
components: Same top masthead

Property header with a kicker showing current pipeline stage, the address as headline, a line of architectural pedigree (architect, year, style), reporter byline with date, and a 'Follow' bookmark button
Stats strip across the top showing list price, price-per-square-foot, lot size, bedrooms, bathrooms, year built, and HOA — each as a label-and-value pair

Two-column body — left is the reading column with subheads, paragraphs, pull quotes, and inline photos with captions; right is a sticky sidebar with a price-history list (date, event, price, delta) and three comparable-property mini-cards

Footer block with a horizontal timeline marking the property's pipeline history (listed, price cut, open house, offer, escrow, closed) and a 'Related dossiers in this neighborhood' strip of three cards

pages.name: neighborhoods
pages.description: Index of neighborhoods the magazine covers, with at-a-glance market data
components: Same top masthead
Section header with the title 'Neighborhoods', a one-sentence description of the section's editorial scope, and a city-tab row (San Francisco, Brooklyn, Lisbon, Mexico City, Kyoto)

Featured neighborhood banner — wide photograph on the left, on the right a neighborhood name, an essay excerpt, a 'Read the field report' link, and a four-cell mini-stat grid (median price, inventory, days-on-market, year-over-year change)

Grid of neighborhood cards (three per row) — each card has a thumbnail, neighborhood name, parent city, a two-line editorial blurb, a small sparkline labeled 'median price, 12 months', and an active-listings count
Footer (same as the board page)

pages.name: archive
pages.description: Searchable archive of past dossiers, sortable as an editorial index
components: Same top masthead

Archive header with title 'The Archive', a one-line description, and a control row containing a search input, a year dropdown, a market dropdown, an outcome filter (Sold, Withdrawn, Still Listed), and a sort dropdown
Index table with columns Date, Address, Market, Architect, Final Outcome, Final Price, Reporter — rows alternate surface tint and each row's address is a link to the dossier
Side panel titled 'Editor's picks from the archive' showing five hand-selected past dossiers as stacked mini-cards (thumbnail, address, one-line note from the editor)
Pagination bar with page numbers and a 'Jump to year' control

pages.name: about
pages.description: About page explaining the publication's premise and introducing the editorial team
components: Same top masthead
Manifesto block with the heading 'Why we track buildings like stories' and three paragraphs of editorial statement
Methodology section laid out as a numbered three-step list (How we choose properties, How we report, How we update the board) — each step has a heading and a paragraph
Masthead grid (three per row) of editors and contributors — each entry has a portrait, name, role, and a one-line bio with a city tag
Contact block with tips email, press email, and a postal address, followed by the standard footer
